verdicts.note: Verified in cached roll calls: Yea on ESSB 6346 House final passage (51-46) and ESSB 5813; multiple 2025 revenue votes [S5-S8] plus a town-hall defense of the income tax [S4]. Second independent sources exist, so +2/high is allowed.

Verified Yea on EHB 1217 third reading and conference report (she voted Nay on concurring in the Senate amendments before conference, consistent with the dossier). One vote plus the pamphlet's eviction-rate framing supports +1/medium.
Verified Yea on ESHB 1469 (2023) and ESSB 5599 (2023) in cached roll calls [S14][S15].
Cached final bill report lists her as original prime sponsor of ESHB 1296 [S10]; her yes votes on it and ESSB 5181 [S11][S13] and ESHB 2331 [S12] make +2/high solid.

Thin and indirect. The pamphlet line 'While they attack our neighbors, I stand with them' [S1] does not name immigrants or immigration enforcement; the dossier's reading is an inference. The only explicit item is a one-phrase campaign claim of having 'pushed for... new protections for immigrant workers' [S2], which is labor policy rather than the axis's ICE/sanctuary/legal-pathways core. Direction is plausible, but that is not a single clear statement on the axis.

Inferred from bill choice, not a stated position on the axis. An infertility insurance-coverage mandate (HB 1730) and dental capital funding [S2] are incremental, but neither says anything for or against universal public coverage, and the axis asks which of those she favors. Without a statement on single-payer or a public option, this is indirect evidence; low confidence.

The only evidence is one generic campaign phrase, 'protecting hardworking families from unnecessary taxes' [S2]. 'Unnecessary' sets no position. He has no stated view on the income tax, I-645 or any revenue proposal. Direction is plausible, but this is not a clear statement on the axis.

Two separate statements: a pamphlet pledge to ensure tax dollars 'are used efficiently' [S1] and the site's 'classroom success, not bureaucracy' [S2]. Both are general but point toward audit and restraint. His 'fix school funding at the source' does not clearly mean more spending, so -1/medium holds.
No elected experience, 'not a career politician' [S1], and he lost his only earlier race in 2025 by a wide margin [S3][S5]. Facing a ten-year incumbent, +2/medium fits.
